Age of onset (25 years) falls within the typical window for schizophrenia spectrum disorders. While the belief is idiosyncratic and not bizarre *in the strictest DSM-5 sense* (some might argue telepathy is not *impossible*—though scientifically implausible—it is still delusional given the conviction, incorrigibility, and functional impact), the persistence (>6 months), associated behavioral disorganization (bizarre dress, ritualized attempts at telepathy), and impairment in insight/judgment strongly support a primary psychotic disorder. Schizophreniform disorder requires symptoms <6 months; this has lasted 8 months → rules it out. Delusional disorder requires non-bizarre delusions *only*, with otherwise intact functioning—but his behavior (burlap attire, public telepathic attempts) and functional context (working at a health food store may accommodate eccentricity, but the degree of conviction and behavioral expression suggests more than isolated delusion) make this less likely. Schizotypal personality disorder involves enduring traits, not an active, impairing episode with recent onset and duration >6 months—this presentation is better characterized as an active psychotic disorder. Therefore, the most appropriate diagnosis is schizophrenia, paranoid or mixed type, given the presence of delusions (telepathic ability/loss) and disorganized behavior, with duration >6 months, absence of prominent mood episodes, and no organic etiology identified.

DIAGNOSIS: Schizophrenia
